name: Positional Numeral System (Hindu-Arabic Numerals)
summary: Base-10 positional notation with zero, originating in India, transmitted through Islamic scholarship, enabling efficient arithmetic, algebra, and modern computation.

claims.statement: Positional notation with zero made arithmetic operations orders of magnitude faster than Roman or Greek numeral systems
Al-Khwarizmi's treatise transmitted Indian numerals to the Islamic world and eventually Europe, enabling the rise of algebra and bookkeeping
The system was independently replicated across every literate civilization within 800 years of its creation, displacing all competing notations

evidence.source: Brahmagupta (628 CE) Brahmasphutasiddhanta, first systematic rules for zero and negative numbers
Ifrah (2000) The Universal History of Numbers, Wiley
Al-Khwarizmi (c. 825 CE) On the Calculation with Hindu Numerals, translated by Vogel (1963)
Robson (2008) Mathematics in Ancient Iraq: A Social History, Princeton UP
Plofker (2009) Mathematics in India, Princeton UP

notes: A keystone information technology that crosses cultural boundaries: Indian origin, Islamic transmission, European adoption. Demonstrates the mosaic principle — no single culture completed the stack alone.
